overall: Reissued on reconsideration (clarifying the dated video and photo evidence): the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by muting its audio during part of the November 30, 2020 meeting; other allegations were declined or not reached as untimely. Only future compliance was ordered.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board's members were inaudible to the public during the November 30, 2020 remote-access meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Since the Board was muted during at least some portion of the Board’s November 30 meeting while discussions were ongoing, we find that the meeting was not open and accessible to the public, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board was inaudible during an October 19, 2020 meeting, which the AG found was filed more than 30 days after it could have been discovered.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review Mr. Komosa’s allegation that he also could not hear the Board at an October 19 meeting, because that alleged violation could have been discovered at the time the meeting took place, which was more than 30 days before this complaint was filed.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board approved inaccurate minutes of its October 19, 2020 meeting; the AG declined because the minutes were approved more than 30 days before filing.
allegations.key_passage: We also decline to review Mr. Komosa’s allegation that the Board approved inaccurate meeting minutes of Board’s October 19 meeting, as the October 19 meeting minutes were approved on November 2.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board intentionally muted its audio at meetings from August 2020 onward and relied on staff to relay answers; untimely, so not investigated.
allegations.key_passage: As this complaint was not filed within 30 days of those meetings, we did not investigate this allegation and make no specific finding as to whether the Board violated the Law in this respect.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
